subject: Math
prompt:
The function f is defined by f(x)=p(3.5x+3.5q), where p and q are integer constants and 0<p<q. The functions u and v are equivalent to function f, where n and r are constants. Which of the following equations displays the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the graph of y=f(x) in the xy-plane as a constant or coefficient?

I. u(x)=p(3.5x+n)

II. v(x)=p(3.5)x+r
explanation:
Choice D is correct. The y-intercept of the graph is found by substituting $x = 0$ into $f(x) = p\left(3.5^{x} + 3.5^{q}\right)$, giving $f(0) = p\left(1 + 3.5^{q}\right) = p + p(3.5)^{q}$. So the y-coordinate of the y-intercept is $p + p(3.5)^{q}$.

For function $u(x) = p\left(3.5^{x} + n\right)$ to be equivalent to $f$, we must have $n = 3.5^{q}$. Since $0 < p$ and $q > 0$, neither the coefficient $p$ nor the constant $n = 3.5^{q}$ equals $p + p(3.5)^{q}$ (because $p(3.5)^{q} \neq 0$). So $u$ does not display the y-coordinate as a constant or coefficient.

For function $v(x) = p(3.5)^{x} + r$ to be equivalent to $f$, rewriting $f(x) = p(3.5)^{x} + p(3.5)^{q}$ gives $r = p(3.5)^{q}$. Neither the coefficient $p$ nor the constant $r = p(3.5)^{q}$ equals $p + p(3.5)^{q}$. So $v$ does not display the y-coordinate as a constant or coefficient.

Therefore, neither I nor II displays the y-coordinate of the y-intercept as a constant or coefficient.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. In $u(x) = p\left(3.5^{x} + n\right)$, the constant $n$ equals $3.5^{q}$, not the y-coordinate of the y-intercept $p + p(3.5)^{q}$, and the coefficient $p$ also does not equal this y-coordinate.
